Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City MR. JOB. B FERNANDEZ HR Officer/LegaI http: Ilwvvw.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION NO. 14 OCT 2019 Goodlife Damayan Insurance Agency Co. National Highways, San Jose Digos City, Davao del Sur Dear Mr. Fernandez: This has reference to your letter dated 18 June 2019, requesting the Department to render legal opinion on whether or not a Certificate of Authority as Insurance Company is a requirement for an Insurance Agency to apply for a Business Permit. Per your letter and the attached certificates, GOODLIFE DAMAYAN INSURANCE AGENCY CO. is an accredited insurance agent of CLIMBS LIFE AND GENERAL INSURANCE COOPERATIVE. Due to the massive expansion of the operation of the former, you desire to establish a branch office in Mati City, Davao Oriental. However, the BPLO of Mati City did not accept your application for business permit as they require you to submit a Certificate of Authority, referring to the Department's Memorandum Circular No. 2017-29, dated IO February 2019. Stated in the said MC is a part of Section 193 of Republic Act No. 10607, otherwise known as the "Insurance Code", to wit: "No insurance company issued with a valid certificate of authority to transact insurance business anywhere in the Philippines by the Insurance Commissioner, shall be barred, prevented, or disenfranchised from issuing any insurance policy or from transacting any insurance business within the scope or coverage of its certificate of authority, anywhere in the Philippines, by any local government unit or authority, for whatever guise or reason whatsoever, including under any kind of ordinance, accreditation system, or scheme. Any local ordinance or local government unit regulatory issuance imposing such restriction or disenfranchisement on any insurance company shall be deemed null and void ab initio. " May we note that the afore-quoted provision of the Code mentioned insurance company, but not insurance agency.

On the other hand, Section 192 of the same Code provides: "SEC. 192. No corporation, partnership, or association of persons shall transact any insurance business in the Philippines except as agent of a CQrperation. r hi r ass ci -z business of insurance in the Philippines unless possessed of the capital and assets required of an insurance corporation doing the same kind of business in the Philippines and invested in the same manner; unless the Commissioner shall have granted it a certificate to the effect that it has complied with all the provisions of this Code. " xxx (Emphasis supplied) Per the above-mentioned provisions of the Insurance Code, certificate of authority to transact business anywhere in the Philippines is issued to: (I) Insurance Company, and (2) agents of insurance business, if the Commissioner granted them a certificate to the effect that it has complied with all the provisions of the Insurance Code. The attached CERTIFICATE issued by the Insurance Commission on 31 August 2018 in favor of GOODLIFE DAMAYAN INSURANCE AGENCY CO. reveals that the latter is an accredited agent of CLIMBS LIFE AND GENERAL INSURANCE COOPERATIVE, an insurance company issued with a certificate of authority (attached in the letter). Therefore, not yet issued a certificate of authority as contemplated in number 2 above. Accordingly, the Department concurs with the Regional Office of Insurance Commission that the document attached in your letter, such as: (I) CERTIFICATION issued by the Insurance Commission on 31 August 2018, (2) CERTIFICATION issued by CLIMBS LIFE AND GENERAL INSURANCE COOPERATIVE, and (3) Certificate of Authority issued in favor of Climbs Life already suffices. We hope we have assisted you on the matter. Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: MARIVEL C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Undersecretary CC: Dir. Alex C. Roldan Regional Director DILG-Region X1 Ls/90 O/
